title.zh: 卷298 列傳八十五 噶尔弼 法喇 查克丹 钦拜 常赉 哈元生 哈尚德 董芳 查弼纳 达福 定寿 素图
title.en: Volume 298 Biographies 85: Ga Er Bi, Fa La, Cha Kedan, Qin Bai, Chang Lai, Ha Yuan Sheng, Ha Shang De, Dong Fang, Cha Bina, Da Fu, Ding Shou, Su Tu
title.raw: 卷298 列傳八十五 噶尔弼 法喇 查克丹 钦拜 常赉 哈元生 哈尚德 董芳 查弼纳 达福 定寿 素图

sentences.zh: 噶爾弼，納喇氏，滿洲鑲紅旗人。

translations.literal: Garbi, of the Nara clan, was a bannerman of the Manchu Bordered Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Garbi of the Nara clan belonged to the Manchu Bordered Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 父額爾德赫，為敬謹親王尼堪長史，屢從征伐。

translations.literal: His father Eerdehe served as chief steward to Prince Jingjin Nikang and repeatedly accompanied campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: His father Eerdehe had been chief steward to Prince Jingjin Nikang and often went on campaign with him.

sentences.zh: 順治十六年，署護軍統領。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Shunzhi he served as acting commandant of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 16 he was appointed acting commandant of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 偕安南將軍達素等師下廈門，擊鄭成功。

translations.literal: Together with An'nan General Dasu and others he led troops down to Xiamen to attack Zheng Chenggong.
translations.idiomatic: He joined An'nan General Dasu and others in leading an army to Xiamen against Zheng Chenggong.

sentences.zh: 額爾德赫將右翼，獲其將周序。

translations.literal: Eerdehe commanded the right wing and captured Zheng's general Zhou Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Eerdehe led the right wing and took Zheng's general Zhou Xu prisoner.

sentences.zh: 命署鎮海將軍。

translations.literal: He was ordered to serve as acting Zhenhai General.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed acting Zhenhai General.

sentences.zh: 康熙元年，還京，尋卒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kangxi he returned to the capital and soon died.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 1 he returned to Beijing and died shortly afterward.

sentences.zh: 雍正間，以噶爾弼疏乞補諡，諡果毅。

translations.literal: During the Yongzheng reign, on Garbi's memorial requesting a posthumous title for him, [Eerdehe] was given the posthumous name Guoyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongzheng era Garbi petitioned for a posthumous title for his father, who was posthumously named Guoyi.

sentences.zh: 噶爾弼，初授前鋒參領，累遷鑲紅旗護軍統領。

translations.literal: Garbi was first appointed vanguard commandant-in-chief and was repeatedly promoted to commandant of the Bordered Red Banner Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Garbi began as vanguard commandant-in-chief and rose step by step to commandant of the Bordered Red Banner Guard.

sentences.zh: 準噶爾策妄阿喇布坦遣策零敦多卜襲據西藏，康熙五十八年，命噶爾弼馳赴四川佐總督年羹堯治軍事。

translations.literal: When Tsewang Arabtan of the Dzungars sent Tsering Dondob to seize Tibet, in the fifty-eighth year of Kangxi the Emperor ordered Garbi to hasten to Sichuan to assist Governor-General Nian Gengyao in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 58, after Tsewang Arabtan dispatched Tsering Dondob to occupy Tibet, the Emperor sent Garbi posthaste to Sichuan to help Governor-General Nian Gengyao with the war.

sentences.zh: 噶爾弼诇知策零敦多卜與其副三濟不睦，謂其隙可乘，疏請招策零敦多卜降。

translations.literal: Garbi learned that Tsering Dondob was at odds with his deputy Sanji-bu, judged the rift could be exploited, and memorialized asking to win Tsering Dondob over to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Garbi discovered that Tsering Dondob and his lieutenant Sanji-bu were estranged, argued the breach could be turned to advantage, and asked permission to induce Tsering Dondob to defect.

sentences.zh: 五十九年二月，上命平逆將軍延信自青海入西藏，而授噶爾弼定西將軍，偕都統武格將四川、雲南兵出拉里。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fifty-ninth year the Emperor ordered Pacification General Yanxin to enter Tibet from Qinghai, while appointing Garbi General Dingxi and having him join Commander-in-chief Wu Ge in leading Sichuan and Yunnan troops out from Lari.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Kangxi 59 the Emperor ordered Yanxin, Pacification General of the West, into Tibet from Qinghai and made Garbi General Dingxi, with Wu Ge, to march Sichuan and Yunnan forces from Lari.

sentences.zh: 策零敦多卜自將拒延信，而遣其黨春丕勒宰桑將二千六百人自章米爾戎拒噶爾弼。

translations.literal: Tsering Dondob personally led forces to resist Yanxin, while dispatching his follower Chunpille zaisang with 2,600 men from Zhangmi'er Rong to block Garbi.
translations.idiomatic: Tsering Dondob himself opposed Yanxin while sending his partisan Chunpille zaisang with 2,600 troops from Zhangmi'er Rong to hold Garbi off.

sentences.zh: 噶爾弼取間道至莫珠貢喀，集皮船渡河，直趨西藏，八月，克之。

translations.literal: Garbi took a bypath to Mozhu gongka, assembled skin rafts to cross the river, and pressed straight into Tibet; in the eighth month he took it.
translations.idiomatic: Garbi stole along a side route to Mozhu gongka, ferried his men on hide boats, and drove straight into Tibet, which he recovered in the eighth month.

sentences.zh: 噶爾弼集西藏大小第巴、頭目及諸寺喇嘛宣上指安撫，封達賴喇嘛倉庫，遣兵守隘，截準噶爾糧道，擒斬策零敦多卜所署置總管喇嘛五。

translations.literal: Garbi assembled Tibet's senior and junior diba, local chiefs, and lamas of the various monasteries to proclaim the Emperor's instructions and reassure them; he sealed the Dalai Lama's storehouses, posted troops to guard the passes, cut the Dzungar grain routes, and captured and executed five chief steward lamas appointed by Tsering Dondob.
translations.idiomatic: Garbi gathered Tibet's great and petty diba, headmen, and monastery lamas to announce the throne's will and calm the people; he sealed the Dalai Lama's granaries, garrisoned the defiles, severed Dzungar supply lines, and killed five steward lamas Tsering Dondob had installed.

sentences.zh: 策零敦多卜為延信所破，遁走。

translations.literal: Tsering Dondob was defeated by Yanxin and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Tsering Dondob was broken by Yanxin and fled.

sentences.zh: 西藏平。

translations.literal: Tibet was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet was pacified.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，上諭曰：「噶爾弼等遵朕指行師絕域，各自奮勵，撫定唐古特人民，命優敘。」

translations.literal: When news of victory arrived, the Emperor issued instructions, saying: "Garbi and the others, following My orders, marched into distant lands; each strove vigorously and brought peace to the Tangut people. Order them specially commended."
translations.idiomatic: When victory was reported, the Emperor said: "Garbi and his officers, obeying My command in campaigning beyond the frontier, had each exerted themselves to pacify the Tangut peoples. Let them be rewarded in full."

sentences.zh: 延信留駐西藏，六十年，以病召還，命噶爾弼佩定西將軍往代。

translations.literal: Yanxin remained garrisoned in Tibet. In the sixtieth year [of Kangxi], recalled because of illness, [the Emperor] ordered Garbi, wearing the title General Dingxi, to go and replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Yanxin stayed on in Tibet. In Kangxi 60 he was recalled for illness, and Garbi was sent back as General Dingxi to take his place.

sentences.zh: 尋授鑲藍旗蒙古都統。

translations.literal: He was soon appointed Mongol commander-in-chief of the Bordered Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Mongol commander-in-chief of the Bordered Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 行至瀘定橋，託病不行。

translations.literal: When he reached Luding Bridge he pleaded illness and would not proceed.
translations.idiomatic: At Luding Bridge he claimed sickness and refused to go on.

sentences.zh: 年羹堯以聞，命奪官；

translations.literal: Nian Gengyao reported this, and [the Emperor] ordered his dismissal;
translations.idiomatic: Nian Gengyao reported it, and the Emperor stripped him of office;

sentences.zh: 逗遛不敢詣京師，論斬。

translations.literal: he lingered and dared not go to the capital; he was sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: he dallied, afraid to come to court, and was condemned to decapitation.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，世宗貰其罪，賜都統銜從軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng the Shizong Emperor pardoned his crime and granted him the rank of commander-in-chief to follow the army.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 1 the Yongzheng Emperor excused his offense and gave him a commander-in-chief's title for field service.

sentences.zh: 迭署固原提督、布隆吉爾副將軍，授鑲紅旗漢軍都統。

translations.literal: He served in succession as acting Guyuan provincial military commander, Bulongji'er deputy general, and commander-in-chief of the Bordered Red Banner Chinese Army.
translations.idiomatic: He acted in turn as Guyuan provincial commander, Bulongji'er deputy general, and commander-in-chief of the Bordered Red Chinese Banner.

sentences.zh: 三年，擢奉天將軍。

translations.literal: In the third year he was promoted to Fengtian General.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he became Fengtian General.

sentences.zh: 五年，疏言：「奉天金、銀、銅、鉛諸礦，雖開採有禁，而竊掘尚多。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he memorialized: "In Fengtian, gold, silver, copper, and lead mines are forbidden to be worked, yet illicit digging is still frequent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he wrote: "Though mining of gold, silver, copper, and lead in Fengtian is prohibited, secret digging remains common.

sentences.zh: 惟杯犀湖產鐵，為民間農器所需。

translations.literal: Only at Lake Beixi is iron produced, which the people need for farm tools.
translations.idiomatic: Only the iron at Beixi Lake is needed for peasant implements.

sentences.zh: 遼陽黃波羅峪、開原打金廠，請視錦州大悲嶺例，永禁開採。」

translations.literal: At Huangboluo Valley in Liaoyang and Dakaijinchang in Kaiyuan, I ask that mining be permanently forbidden, following the precedent of Dabei Ridge at Jinzhou."
translations.idiomatic: For Huangboluo Valley in Liaoyang and Dakaijinchang in Kaiyuan, I request a permanent ban on mining, as at Dabei Ridge in Jinzhou."

sentences.zh: 下部議行。

translations.literal: The ministry deliberated and carried it out.
translations.idiomatic: The Board approved and implemented the plan.

sentences.zh: 旋卒。

translations.literal: He soon died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after.

sentences.zh: 法喇，那木都魯氏，滿洲正白旗人。

translations.literal: Fala, of the Namuduru clan, was a bannerman of the Manchu Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Fala of the Namuduru clan came from the Manchu Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 父敦泰，從達素擊鄭成功，戰死。

translations.literal: His father Duntai followed Dasu in attacking Zheng Chenggong and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: His father Duntai followed Dasu against Zheng Chenggong and was killed in action.

sentences.zh: 母喜塔臘氏，守節撫孤。

translations.literal: His mother, of the Xitala clan, kept her chastity and raised the orphan.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, a Xitala woman, preserved her widowhood and reared the boy alone.

sentences.zh: 法喇，初授筆帖式。

translations.literal: Fala was first appointed a clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Fala began as a clerk.

sentences.zh: 康熙十三年，以護軍從討吳三桂，自廣東下雲南。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Kangxi he served as a guardsman in the campaign against Wu Sangui, advancing from Guangdong into Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 13 he joined the guards in the expedition against Wu Sangui, marching from Guangdong into Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，以署驍騎參領從征噶爾丹，累擢鑲白旗蒙古都統、護軍統​​領。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year, as acting commandant of the Vanguard Cavalry he joined the campaign against Galdan and was repeatedly promoted to Mongol commander-in-chief of the Bordered White Banner and commandant of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 35, as acting vanguard cavalry commandant, he campaigned against Galdan and rose to Mongol commander-in-chief of the Bordered White Banner and commandant of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 準噶爾策妄阿喇布坦遣其族兄策零敦多卜攻西藏，四川提督康泰率師次黃勝關，兵譁潰。

translations.literal: Tsewang Arabtan of the Dzungars sent his clansman Tsering Dondob to attack Tibet; Sichuan Provincial Military Commander Kang Tai led his army to Huangsheng Pass, where the troops mutinied and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Tsewang Arabtan sent his kinsman Tsering Dondob against Tibet; Sichuan commander Kang Tai halted at Huangsheng Pass, and his army mutinied and broke.

sentences.zh: 上命法喇馳赴四川佐年羹堯治軍事，並按提督標兵譁潰狀。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Fala to hasten to Sichuan to assist Nian Gengyao in military affairs and to investigate the mutiny of the provincial troops under the commander's standard.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent Fala posthaste to Sichuan to aid Nian Gengyao and to inquire into the rout of the provincial brigade.

sentences.zh: 法喇察知泰偏信守備汪文藻克餉，請斬文藻及倡亂兵以徇，上從之，並奪泰官。

translations.literal: Fala found that Kang Tai had been partial to Assistant Commander Wang Wenzao, who withheld rations, and asked to execute Wenzao and the mutinous soldiers as an example; the Emperor agreed and also dismissed Kang Tai.
translations.idiomatic: Fala learned Kang Tai had favored assistant Wang Wenzao, who embezzled pay, and asked that Wenzao and the ringleaders be executed; the throne assented and removed Kang Tai.

sentences.zh: 五十七年，策零敦多卜戕拉藏汗，幽達賴喇嘛，遂據有其地。

translations.literal: In the fifty-seventh year Tsering Dondob killed the Dalai-supporting king Lozang Khan, imprisoned the Dalai Lama, and seized the region.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 57 Tsering Dondob murdered Lozang Khan, confined the Dalai Lama, and occupied Tibet.

sentences.zh: 法喇遣員外郎巴特瑪等赴里塘傳諭，又令前鋒參領伍林葩、化林協副將趙宏基將滿、漢兵五百與之偕。

translations.literal: Fala dispatched Clerk Batma and others to Litang to proclaim the imperial will, and ordered Vanguard Commandant Wulinba and Deputy Commander Zhao Hongji to lead 500 Manchu and Chinese troops with them.
translations.idiomatic: Fala sent Batma and other clerks to Litang with an edict, and detached Vanguard Commandant Wulinba and Deputy Commander Zhao Hongji with 500 banner and Chinese troops.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「西藏資茶養生，應令松潘禁茶出口。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "Tibet depends on tea for livelihood; Songpan should be ordered to forbid tea exports.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote: "Tibet lives on tea; exports from Songpan should be stopped.

sentences.zh: 里塘、巴塘番寨所需，當開具戶口，定數買運。」

translations.literal: For the Tibetan stockades at Litang and Batang, household registers should be drawn up and fixed quotas set for purchase and transport."
translations.idiomatic: For Litang and Batang, household lists should be filed and rationed tea caravans allowed."

sentences.zh: 下所司議行。

translations.literal: The responsible offices deliberated and carried it out.
translations.idiomatic: The yamen approved and enforced the rule.

sentences.zh: 五十八年，命法喇出駐打箭爐，令副將岳鍾琪率師徇里塘，番酋達瓦喇扎木巴、第巴塞卜騰阿珠不從命，縛送法喇軍，斬以徇。

translations.literal: In the fifty-eighth year the Emperor ordered Fala to station at Dajianlu and had Deputy Commander Yue Zhongqi lead troops to secure Litang; the Tibetan chiefs Dawa Razhamuba and the diba Sebeteng Azhu disobeyed, were bound and sent to Fala's camp, and executed as an example.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 58 Fala was posted at Dajianlu; Yue Zhongqi advanced on Litang, and chiefs Dawa Razhamuba and diba Sebeteng Azhu, who resisted, were bound, sent to Fala, and beheaded.

sentences.zh: 進次巴塘，第巴喀木布等請降，命法喇進駐巴塘。

translations.literal: Advancing to Batang, the diba Kamubu and others asked to surrender, and Fala was ordered forward to garrison Batang.
translations.idiomatic: At Batang, diba Kamubu and others submitted, and Fala was told to move his headquarters there.

sentences.zh: 五十九年，年羹堯請授噶爾弼定西將軍，率師入西藏，令法喇還駐打箭爐。

translations.literal: In the fifty-ninth year Nian Gengyao asked that Garbi be made General Dingxi to lead troops into Tibet, and that Fala return to garrison Dajianlu.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 59 Nian Gengyao proposed Garbi as General Dingxi for the Tibetan advance while Fala fell back to Dajianlu.

sentences.zh: 六十年，還京師。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 60 he came back to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 尋以護軍有自戕者，不以實奏，坐奪官。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, because a guardsman had killed himself and he had not reported it truthfully, he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly after, he lost his post for concealing a guardsman's suicide.

sentences.zh: 六十一年，與千叟宴，賜復原銜。

translations.literal: In the sixty-first year he attended the Thousand-Elder banquet and was granted restoration of his former rank.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 61 he joined the Thousand-Elder feast and had his rank restored.

sentences.zh: 雍正十三年，卒。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Yongzheng he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Yongzheng 13.

sentences.zh: 查克丹，博爾濟吉特氏，滿洲正黃旗人，奉義公恩格德爾曾孫。

translations.literal: Chakedan, of the Borjigit clan, was a bannerman of the Manchu Plain Yellow Banner and great-grandson of the Duke of Fengyi Engedeer.
translations.idiomatic: Chakedan, Borjigit of the Plain Yellow Banner, was Engedeer's great-grandson.

sentences.zh: 自官學生襲三等阿達哈哈番，授頭等侍衛。

translations.literal: As a student of the Imperial School he inherited a third-rank adaha fan and was appointed first-class bodyguard.
translations.idiomatic: From the Imperial School he inherited a third-rank adaha fan and became a first-class bodyguard.

sentences.zh: 累遷正黃旗護軍統領、鑲藍旗蒙古都統。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to commandant of the Plain Yellow Banner Guard and Mongol commander-in-chief of the Bordered Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to commandant of the Plain Yellow Guard and Mongol commander-in-chief of the Bordered Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 雍正三年，署甘州將軍。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongzheng he served as acting Ganzhou General.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 3 he acted as Ganzhou General.

sentences.zh: 準噶爾使至，守備馬德仁等供應失時，查克丹疏劾，並陳花馬池至甘州驛馬疲羸狀，命總督年羹堯嚴察。

translations.literal: When Dzungar envoys arrived, Assistant Commander Ma Deren and others failed to supply them in time; Chakedan memorialized against them and also reported the exhaustion of relay horses from Huamachi to Ganzhou, and the Emperor ordered Governor-General Nian Gengyao to investigate strictly.
translations.idiomatic: Dzungar envoys came while Ma Deren and other assistants were late with provisions; Chakedan impeached them and described worn relay horses from Huamachi to Ganzhou, and Nian Gengyao was told to look into it.

sentences.zh: 四年，還京師，授正黃旗滿洲都統。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he returned to the capital and was appointed Manchu commander-in-chief of the Plain Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he returned to court as Plain Yellow Manchu commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 五年，命率番代兵出北路。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was ordered to lead Fan and Dai troops out on the northern route.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was sent north with Fan and Dai auxiliaries.

sentences.zh: 九年，振武將軍順承郡王錫保出北路討準噶爾，命查克丹參贊軍務，授內大臣。

translations.literal: In the ninth year General Zhenwu, Prince Shuncheng Xibao, marched on the northern route against the Dzungars, and Chakedan was ordered to assist in military affairs and was appointed inner court minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Prince Shuncheng Xibao, General Zhenwu, took the northern army against the Dzungars; Chakedan joined his staff as inner minister.

sentences.zh: 十年，準噶爾將小策零敦多卜入邊，掠喀爾喀諸部。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the Dzungar general Little Tsering Dondob crossed the border and raided the Khalkha tribes.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Little Tsering Dondob invaded and plundered the Khalkha.

sentences.zh: 查克丹偕額駙策棱等赴奔博圖山，敵越察罕廋爾入掠杭愛山，師逐之，至額爾德尼昭，大戰破敵。

translations.literal: Chakedan joined the imperial son-in-law Tsering and others at Benbotu Mountain; the enemy crossed Chahan Or to raid Hangai Mountain, and the army pursued them to Erdeni Zhao and routed them in a great battle.
translations.idiomatic: Chakedan with Tsering and others reached Benbotu; the foe crossed Chahan Or into Hangai, was chased to Erdeni Zhao, and crushed.

sentences.zh: 查克丹督兵奮擊，敵自推河遁走；

translations.literal: Chakedan directed the troops in fierce attack, and the enemy fled by way of the Tui River;
translations.idiomatic: Chakedan drove the charge; the enemy escaped down the Tui River;

sentences.zh: 复追至察罕托輝，斬馘殆盡。

translations.literal: they pursued again to Chahan Tuohui and killed nearly all of them.
translations.idiomatic: the pursuit continued to Chahan Tuohui and left few alive.

sentences.zh: 以功進二等阿達哈哈番。

translations.literal: For his merit he was advanced to second-rank adaha fan.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was raised to second-rank adaha fan.

sentences.zh: 錫保代傅爾丹為靖邊大將軍，仍以查克丹參贊軍務。

translations.literal: When Xibao replaced Fu Erdan as Pacification General of the Frontier, Chakedan still assisted in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Xibao succeeded Fu Erdan as frontier commander, Chakedan remained on his staff.

sentences.zh: 十三年，還京師，調正紅旗蒙古都統。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he returned to the capital and was transferred to Mongol commander-in-chief of the Bordered Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he came home and was shifted to Bordered Red Mongol commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四年，以病再疏乞休，命致仕。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Qianlong, ill and having memorialized twice to retire, he was ordered to leave office.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 4, after repeated pleas of illness, he was allowed to retire.

sentences.zh: 十一年，卒，賜祭葬，諡敏恪。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he died; funeral sacrifices were granted and he was given the posthumous name Minke.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 11 he died; the court granted funeral rites and the posthumous name Minke.

sentences.zh: 欽拜，瓜爾佳氏，滿洲鑲紅旗人。

translations.literal: Qinbai, of the Guwalgiya clan, was a bannerman of the Manchu Bordered Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Qinbai of the Guwalgiya clan served in the Bordered Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 曾祖羅璧，勞薩弟也，偕來歸。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Luobi was younger brother to Laosa; they came over together in submission.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestor Luobi, Laosa's brother, had surrendered together with him.

sentences.zh: 有功，授一等阿達哈哈番，以兼襲兄子程尼世職，合為一等公。

translations.literal: For merit he was granted first-rank adaha fan; inheriting his elder brother's son Cheni's office as well, the two were combined as first-rank duke.
translations.idiomatic: Luobi earned first-rank adaha fan and, by also inheriting his brother's son Cheni's post, held a combined first-rank dukedom.

sentences.zh: 欽拜改襲一等伯，授頭等侍衛。

translations.literal: Qinbai changed his inheritance to first-rank earl and was appointed first-class bodyguard.
translations.idiomatic: Qinbai took a first-rank earldom and became a first-class bodyguard.

sentences.zh: 累遷正黃旗蒙古副都統。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Mongol lieutenant-general of the Plain Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Plain Yellow Mongol lieutenant-general.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，授兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng he was appointed vice minister of the Board of War.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 1 he became vice minister of War.

sentences.zh: 四年，以引見失儀，上詰責，巧辯，奪官，戍軍台。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, for impropriety at an audience, when the Emperor questioned him he argued cleverly; he was dismissed and sent to garrison the military posts.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was rude at audience, quibbled under rebuke, lost his post, and was exiled to the garrison line.

sentences.zh: 九年，召還，复官。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was recalled and restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was recalled and reinstated.

sentences.zh: 撫遠大將軍馬爾賽出北路討噶爾丹，命欽拜將右衛兵以從，參贊軍務，授內大臣，駐紮克拜達里克。

translations.literal: Pacification General Maersai marched on the northern route against Galdan; Qinbai was ordered to lead the Right Guard troops in attendance, to assist in military affairs, was appointed inner court minister, and was stationed at Zakobaidarik.
translations.idiomatic: When Maersai went north against Galdan, Qinbai led Right Guard forces on his staff as inner minister, stationed at Zakobaidarik.

sentences.zh: 十年，振武將軍順承郡王錫保駐察罕廋爾，奏請移欽拜相佐。

translations.literal: In the tenth year General Zhenwu Prince Shuncheng Xibao was stationed at Chahan Or and memorialized asking to move Qinbai to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Xibao at Chahan Or asked that Qinbai be sent to help him.

sentences.zh: 上諭曰：「馬爾賽治事甚不愜朕意，扎克拜達里克軍中恃欽拜一人，當仍留北路。」

translations.literal: The Emperor instructed: "Maersai handles affairs in a way that greatly fails to satisfy Me; the army at Zakobaidarik relies on Qinbai alone — he should remain on the northern route."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "Maersai displeases Me; Zakobaidarik depends on Qinbai — keep him in the north."

sentences.zh: 準噶爾將小策零敦多卜等自推河走，欽拜等力請追擊，馬爾賽聽敵過，師乃出。

translations.literal: When the Dzungar general Little Tsering Dondob and others fled by the Tui River, Qinbai and others urgently asked to pursue; Maersai let the enemy pass before the army marched out.
translations.idiomatic: Little Tsering Dondob fled down the Tui; Qinbai begged to chase, but Maersai waited until they were gone before moving.

sentences.zh: 既至博木喀喇，令欽拜將七百人進，不及敵而還。

translations.literal: When they reached Bomukala, Maersai ordered Qinbai forward with 700 men; they failed to catch the enemy and returned.
translations.idiomatic: At Bomukala, Maersai sent Qinbai with 700 men; they found no foe and came back.

sentences.zh: 欽拜等疏聞，上誅馬爾賽。

translations.literal: Qinbai and others reported this; the Emperor executed Maersai.
translations.idiomatic: Qinbai reported it, and Maersai was put to death.

sentences.zh: 尋署綏遠將軍。

translations.literal: He soon served as acting Suiyuan General.
translations.idiomatic: He then acted as Suiyuan General.

sentences.zh: 十一年，复署建勳將軍。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he again served as acting Jianxun General.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he again acted as Jianxun General.

sentences.zh: 平郡王福彭代為定邊大將軍，命軍事諮於欽拜。

translations.literal: When Prince Ping Fupeng replaced him as Pacification General of the Frontier, military affairs were to be consulted with Qinbai.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Ping Fupeng became frontier commander, Qinbai was to be consulted on strategy.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，還京師。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 1 he returned to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 出為青州將軍。

translations.literal: He went out as Qingzhou General.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Qingzhou General.

sentences.zh: 還，在內大臣上行走。

translations.literal: On returning he served in the inner court above the rank of minister.
translations.idiomatic: Back at court he walked as inner minister.

sentences.zh: 十二年，卒，賜祭葬，諡肅敏。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he died; funeral sacrifices were granted and he was given the posthumous name Sumin.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 12 he died; funeral rites were granted and he was named Sumin posthumously.

sentences.zh: 常賚，納喇氏，滿洲鑲白旗人，鎮安將軍瑪奇子。

translations.literal: Chang Lai, of the Nara clan, was a bannerman of the Manchu Bordered White Banner and son of Zhen'an General Maqi.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Lai of the Nara clan, son of Zhen'an General Maqi, belonged to the Bordered White Banner.

sentences.zh: 事世宗雍邸。

translations.literal: He served in the Yong Prince's household.
translations.idiomatic: He had served in the Yong Prince's establishment.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，授工部員外郎，遷郎中。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng he was appointed clerk of the Board of Works and was promoted to director.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 1 he entered the Board of Works as a clerk and became a director.

sentences.zh: 二年，調戶部。

translations.literal: In the second year he was transferred to the Board of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he moved to Revenue.

sentences.zh: 三年，授廣東布政使。

translations.literal: In the third year he was appointed Guangdong provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he became Guangdong administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 四年，擢福建巡撫。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was promoted to Fujian governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was made Fujian governor.

sentences.zh: 廣東巡撫楊文乾言福建倉庫虧空，上命文乾清理，即移常賚署廣東巡撫。

translations.literal: Guangdong Governor Yang Wengan reported a deficit in the Fujian granaries; the Emperor ordered Wengan to clear the accounts and at once moved Chang Lai to act as Guangdong governor.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Wengan exposed Fujian treasury shortfalls, the Emperor had Wengan audit them and shifted Chang Lai to acting Guangdong governor.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「廣東地卑苦，夏秋潦漲，廣州、肇慶二府尤甚。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "Guangdong's land is low and suffers hardship; in summer and autumn the floods rise, especially in Guangzhou and Zhaoqing prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote: "Guangdong is low-lying and flood-prone, worst in Guangzhou and Zhaoqing.

sentences.zh: 請以廣州通判管南海、三水堤工，肇慶通判管高要、高明、四會堤工，歲冬督堤長修築，定保固賞罰。

translations.literal: I ask that the Guangzhou subprefect oversee dikes in Nanhai and Sanshui, and the Zhaoqing subprefect those in Gaoyao, Gaoming, and Sihui; each winter the dike chiefs should be supervised in repairs, with fixed rewards and penalties for warranty.
translations.idiomatic: Let the Guangzhou subprefect manage Nanhai and Sanshui embankments and the Zhaoqing subprefect those of Gaoyao, Gaoming, and Sihui, with winter repairs, bonded guarantees, and set rewards and fines.

sentences.zh: 水漲護防，仍以鴨埠、魚諸稅充用。」

translations.literal: When the waters rise they should be guarded; expenses should still be met from the taxes at Yabu, fish weirs, and the like."
translations.idiomatic: When floods come, patrol them; costs should still come from Yabu, fish-weir, and similar levies."

sentences.zh: 尋赴福建。

translations.literal: He soon went to Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon sent to Fujian.

sentences.zh: 六年，調雲南。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was moved to Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 常賚在廣東，盜竊奏摺匣鎖鑰，令工私製；

translations.literal: While Chang Lai was in Guangdong, thieves stole the lock and key of the memorial-case; he had craftsmen make replacements in secret;
translations.idiomatic: In Guangdong, thieves took the memorial-case lock and key, and Chang Lai secretly had copies made;

sentences.zh: 將軍標兵匿盜，徇不治；

translations.literal: the general's standard troops harbored robbers, yet he punished them only as an example without real prosecution;
translations.idiomatic: his general's troops sheltered bandits, which he punished only for show;

sentences.zh: 電白、從化盜發，隱不奏；

translations.literal: when bandits rose at Dianbai and Conghua he concealed it and did not report;
translations.idiomatic: bandit outbreaks at Dianbai and Conghua went unreported;

sentences.zh: 又與將軍石禮哈等訐文乾。

translations.literal: he also joined General Shiliha and others in impeaching Yang Wengan.
translations.idiomatic: he also sided with General Shiliha and others against Yang Wengan.

sentences.zh: 上諭曰：「常賚朕籓邸微員，以其謹慎，擢至巡撫。

translations.literal: The Emperor instructed: "Chang Lai was a petty servant in My princely household; because he was careful, he was raised to governor.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "Chang Lai was a minor clerk in My household; I promoted him to governor for his diligence.

sentences.zh: 乃盜失摺匣鑰匿不奏，尚得謂無欺乎？

translations.literal: Yet when the memorial-case key was stolen he concealed it — can this still be called free of deceit?
translations.idiomatic: He hid the theft of the memorial-case key — how is that honest?

sentences.zh: 且與石禮哈等黨同伐異，其罪不可貸！

translations.literal: Moreover he banded with Shiliha and others to attack those unlike themselves; his crime cannot be pardoned!
translations.idiomatic: Worse, he formed a faction with Shiliha to hound rivals; his guilt is unpardonable!

sentences.zh: 奪官，赴廣東待鞫。」

translations.literal: He was dismissed from office and sent to Guangdong to await trial."
translations.idiomatic: He was stripped of office and sent to Guangdong for trial."

sentences.zh: 論斬，上推瑪奇下雲南舊功，特赦之，令從尚書查弼納往陝西治餉。

translations.literal: He was sentenced to death; the Emperor, weighing Maqi's old merit in Yunnan, specially pardoned him and ordered him to follow Minister Zhabina to Shaanxi to manage supplies.
translations.idiomatic: Condemned to death, he was spared for Maqi's Yunnan service and sent with Zhabina to manage Shaanxi rations.

sentences.zh: 八年，授刑部侍郎，署寧夏將軍。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was appointed vice minister of the Board of Punishments and served as acting Ningxia General.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he became vice minister of Punishments and acting Ningxia General.

sentences.zh: 九年，授鎮安將軍，將肅、甘、涼三州兵五千人自為一隊，備聲援。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was appointed Zhen'an General and led 5,000 troops from Suzhou, Ganzhou, and Liangzhou as an independent detachment for supporting operations.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he became Zhen'an General with 5,000 men from Suzhou, Ganzhou, and Liangzhou as a reserve column.

sentences.zh: 尋授西路副將軍。

translations.literal: He soon was appointed Western Route deputy general.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Western Route deputy general.

sentences.zh: 十年，準噶爾侵哈密，常賚與都統良敦、總兵張存孝將滿、漢兵三千二百，駐無克克嶺御之。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the Dzungars invaded Hami; Chang Lai with Commander-in-chief Liang Dun and Regional Commander Zhang Cunxiao led 3,200 Manchu and Chinese troops to garrison Wukekeling to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, when the Dzungars struck Hami, Chang Lai, Liang Dun, and Zhang Cunxiao with 3,200 banner and Chinese troops held Wukekeling.

sentences.zh: 旋授內大臣。

translations.literal: He was soon appointed inner court minister.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon named inner minister.

sentences.zh: 從大將軍岳鍾琪移軍穆壘，復從護大將軍張廣泗移軍巴爾庫爾。

translations.literal: He followed Grand General Yue Zhongqi in moving the army to Mulei, then followed Protecting General Zhang Guangsi in moving the army to Barkol.
translations.idiomatic: He marched with Yue Zhongqi to Mulei, then with Zhang Guangsi to Barkol.

sentences.zh: 十一年冬，署大將軍查郎阿奏方冬雪深，請分兵駐防，廣泗將萬人駐北山，常賚將九千人駐南山。

translations.literal: In the winter of the eleventh year Acting Grand General Chalang'a memorialized that deep snow had fallen; he asked to divide troops for garrison duty; Guangsi stationed 10,000 men on the northern hills and Chang Lai 9,000 on the southern hills.
translations.idiomatic: In winter of the eleventh year Chalang'a, acting commander, cited deep snow and split the army: Guangsi held the north with 10,000 men, Chang Lai the south with 9,000.

sentences.zh: 十三年，命統綠旗兵萬人駐巴爾庫爾，提督顏清如、尚書馬會伯為副。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was ordered to command 10,000 Green Standard troops at Barkol, with Provincial Military Commander Yan Qingru and Minister Ma Huibo as deputies.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he took 10,000 Green Standard troops at Barkol under Yan Qingru and Ma Huibo.

sentences.zh: 準噶爾乞和，乾隆元年，率兵還京師。

translations.literal: The Dzungars sued for peace; in the first year of Qianlong he led the army back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the Dzungars sued for peace in Qianlong 1 he returned to Beijing with the army.

sentences.zh: 五年，以疾致仕，予半俸。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, ill, he retired and was granted half salary.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 5 illness forced retirement on half pay.

sentences.zh: 十一年，卒，賜祭葬。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he died; funeral sacrifices were granted.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 11 he died and received funeral rites.

sentences.zh: 哈元生，直隸河間人。

translations.literal: Ha Yuansheng was a native of Hejian in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Ha Yuansheng came from Hejian in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 康熙間入伍，授把總。

translations.literal: During the Kangxi reign he entered the army and was appointed platoon leader.
translations.idiomatic: Under Kangxi he enlisted and became a platoon leader.

sentences.zh: 累遷建昌路都司。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to commander of the Jianchang circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Jianchang circuit commander.

sentences.zh: 坐失察私木過關，奪官。

translations.literal: For failure to detect smuggled timber at a pass he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his post for lax inspection of smuggled timber.

sentences.zh: 雍正二年，命引見，發直隸以守備用，補撫標右營守備。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongzheng he was ordered to audience, sent to Zhili for use as assistant commander, and appointed assistant commander of the provincial right battalion.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 2 he was presented at court, sent to Zhili as an assistant commander candidate, and filled the provincial right battalion.

sentences.zh: 貴州威寧總兵石禮哈請以元生從剿仲家苗，有勞，三年，補威寧鎮中軍游擊。

translations.literal: Guizhou Weining General Shiliha asked that Yuansheng join in suppressing the Zhongjia Miao; for his service, in the third year he was appointed acting major of the Weining garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Weining General Shiliha took Yuansheng against the Zhongjia Miao; in the third year he became acting Weining major.

sentences.zh: 烏蒙土知府祿萬鍾侵東川，鎮雄土知府隴慶侯助為亂。

translations.literal: Wuman native prefect Lu Wanzhong invaded Dongchuan, and Zhenxiong native prefect Long Qinghou aided the rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Wuman prefect Lu Wanzhong raided Dongchuan while Zhenxiong prefect Long Qinghou joined the revolt.

sentences.zh: 鄂爾泰檄元生會四川兵討賊，賊據險拒戰，元生冒矢石奪攻克之。

translations.literal: Ortai ordered Yuansheng to join Sichuan troops in attacking the rebels; the rebels held difficult ground and resisted; Yuansheng braved arrows and stones and stormed the position.
translations.idiomatic: Ortai sent Yuansheng with Sichuan forces; the rebels held the heights until Yuansheng stormed them under fire.

sentences.zh: 鄂爾泰上其功，上獎元生取仲家苗、克烏蒙能效力，命以副將、參將題用，尋授尋霑營參將。

translations.literal: Ortai reported his merit; the Emperor praised Yuansheng's effectiveness against the Zhongjia Miao and in taking Wuman, ordered him nominated for lieutenant colonel or colonel, and soon appointed him colonel of the Xunqian garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Ortai praised his work; the throne nominated him for colonel or lieutenant colonel and made him Xunqian colonel.

sentences.zh: 六年，米貼苗婦陸氏為亂，鄂爾泰令元生往剿，破險設伏，搗其巢，獲陸氏。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the Miao woman Lu of Mitie rebelled; Ortai sent Yuansheng to suppress her; he broke through difficult terrain, set ambushes, stormed their nest, and captured Lu.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Lu of Mitie rebelled; Yuansheng ambushed her stronghold and took her prisoner.

sentences.zh: 率師赴阿驢，破雷波土司，以其助陸氏劫糧也。

translations.literal: He led troops to Ali, defeated the Leibo native chieftain for aiding Lu in robbing grain convoys.
translations.idiomatic: At Ali he crushed Leibo's chieftain, who had helped Lu plunder supplies.

sentences.zh: 賚白金四千。

translations.literal: He was rewarded with 4,000 taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: The court gave him 4,000 taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 遷元江副將。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be lieutenant colonel at Yuanjiang.
translations.idiomatic: He became Yuanjiang lieutenant colonel.

sentences.zh: 師還，阿驢夷目從，坐事，元生鞭之，其人大譟，圍元生。

translations.literal: When the army returned, an Ali chieftain followed; for an offense Yuansheng flogged him; the man raised a great outcry and surrounded Yuansheng.
translations.idiomatic: On the march home an Ali headman whom Yuansheng whipped raised a mob and besieged him.

sentences.zh: 元生率游擊卜萬年等與戰兩晝夜，賊敗卻，元生督兵奪據赤衣台。

translations.literal: Yuansheng with Major Bu Wannian and others fought for two days and nights; the rebels were defeated and withdrew; Yuansheng directed the troops to seize Chiyi Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Yuansheng and Major Bu Wannian fought two days and nights, routed the mob, and seized Chiyi Terrace.

sentences.zh: 鶴麗總兵張耀祖赴援，元生出小溜筒江，搜斬餘賊，阿驢人空寨遁。

translations.literal: General Zhang Yaozu of Heli came to the rescue; Yuansheng came out by the Xiaoliutong River, hunted down the remaining rebels, and the Ali people abandoned their stockades and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Heli General Zhang Yaozu relieved him; Yuansheng cleared the Xiaoliutong valley, and Ali villages emptied.

sentences.zh: 拉金、者呢諸寨助為亂，並討平之。

translations.literal: The stockades Lajin and Zhene had aided the rebellion; he pacified them as well.
translations.idiomatic: He also subdued Lajin, Zhene, and other rebel villages.

sentences.zh: 鄂爾泰具以聞，上諭曰：「野夷性反覆，即無鞭責事，亦未必帖然。

translations.literal: Ortai reported in full; the Emperor instructed: "Wild tribes are by nature changeable; even without the whipping affair they would not necessarily have been docile.
translations.idiomatic: Ortai reported; the Emperor said: "Barbarians are fickle; even without the flogging they might have risen.

sentences.zh: 元生效力多，功過相當。

translations.literal: Yuansheng has rendered much service; merit and fault balance.
translations.idiomatic: Yuansheng's services offset his fault.

sentences.zh: 置不議。」

translations.literal: Let the matter be set aside without deliberation."
translations.idiomatic: No further inquiry was needed."

sentences.zh: 七年，調黎平副將，擢安籠總兵。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to be lieutenant colonel at Liping and was promoted to Anlong regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he became Liping lieutenant colonel, then Anlong commander.

sentences.zh: 八年，烏蒙復為亂，鄂爾泰令元生督兵出威寧，破賊數万，射殪其渠黑寡、暮末，連躪賊壘八十里，遂克烏蒙。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Wuman rebelled again; Ortai ordered Yuansheng to lead troops out from Weining, defeat tens of thousands of rebels, shoot dead their leaders Heiguo and Momo, overrun enemy camps for eighty li in succession, and finally take Wuman.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Wuman rose again; Yuansheng from Weining broke tens of thousands of rebels, killed chiefs Heiguo and Momo, swept eighty li of camps, and retook Wuman.

sentences.zh: 賜孔雀翎及冠服，賚白金萬。

translations.literal: He was granted a peacock feather and court dress and rewarded with 10,000 taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: He received a peacock plume, court robes, and 10,000 taels.

sentences.zh: 九年，擢雲南提督。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was promoted to Yunnan provincial military commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he became Yunnan commander.

sentences.zh: 上以元生母逾八十，予封誥。

translations.literal: Because Yuansheng's mother was over eighty, ennoblement patent was granted.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, past eighty, received an honor patent.

sentences.zh: 尋調貴州。

translations.literal: He was soon transferred to Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon shifted to Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 十年，召詣京師，入對，解禦衣以賜，命在辦理軍機處行走。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was summoned to the capital for audience; the Emperor removed his own court robe to bestow it and ordered him to serve in the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was called to court, given the Emperor's own robe, and admitted to the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 旋令回籍省親。

translations.literal: He was soon ordered to return home to visit his parents.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon sent home on leave.

sentences.zh: 貴州九股苗為亂，命還貴州督剿。

translations.literal: The Jiugu Miao of Guizhou rebelled; he was ordered back to Guizhou to supervise suppression.
translations.idiomatic: When Guizhou's Jiugu Miao rebelled, he was sent back to command the campaign.

sentences.zh: 遭母喪，賜祭，令在任守制。

translations.literal: He suffered his mother's death; funeral sacrifices were granted and he was ordered to observe mourning while remaining at his post.
translations.idiomatic: His mother died; mourning rites were granted but he stayed on duty.

sentences.zh: 率兵攻九股苗，獲悍苗百餘，俘斬甚眾，餘悉請降。

translations.literal: He led troops against the Jiugu Miao, captured more than a hundred fierce warriors, killed and took many prisoners, and the rest all asked to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He took a hundred fierce Miao captives, killed many, and the rest surrendered.

sentences.zh: 十二月，進新闢苗疆圖誌，命巡撫元展成勘訂。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he presented a gazetteer of the newly opened Miao frontier and was ordered to have Governor Yuan Zhancheng collate it.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he submitted a gazetteer of the new Miao districts for Yuan Zhancheng to edit.

sentences.zh: 十三年，古州苗為亂，擾黃平，元生遣兵擊之，總督尹繼善奏調湖廣、廣西兵會剿。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year the Guzhou Miao rebelled and disturbed Huangping; Yuansheng sent troops against them; Governor-General Yin Jishan memorialized to assemble Hunan and Guangxi troops for joint suppression.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Guzhou Miao raided Huangping; Yin Jishan called Hunan and Guangxi reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 上授元生為揚威將軍，統兵進討，而以湖廣提督董芳為之副。

translations.literal: The Emperor appointed Yuansheng General Yangwei to command the advance, with Hunan Commander Dong Fang as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor made Yuansheng General Yangwei with Dong Fang as deputy.

sentences.zh: 尋遣尚書張照為撫定苗疆大臣，元生與之忤。

translations.literal: Soon Minister Zhang Zhao was dispatched as Commissioner for Pacifying the Miao Frontier; Yuansheng clashed with him.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Zhang Zhao was sent to pacify the Miao, and Yuansheng quarreled with him.

sentences.zh: 乃議劃施秉以上為上游，用雲南、貴州兵，隸元生；

translations.literal: It was then decided to divide the territory above Shibing as the upper reaches, using Yunnan and Guizhou troops under Yuansheng;
translations.idiomatic: The frontier above Shibing was assigned to Yuansheng with Yunnan and Guizhou troops;

sentences.zh: 施秉以下為下游，用湖廣、廣西兵，隸芳。

translations.literal: below Shibing as the lower reaches, using Hunan and Guangxi troops under Fang.
translations.idiomatic: below Shibing to Fang with Hunan and Guangxi forces.

sentences.zh: 元生與芳議界，詳逮村莊道路，文移辨論，日久師無功。

translations.literal: Yuansheng and Fang debated the boundary, detailing every village and road in documents, and for a long time the army achieved nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Yuansheng and Fang haggled over villages and roads while the campaign stalled.

sentences.zh: 經略張廣泗至，劾元生徒事招撫，奪官逮京師，坐貽誤軍機論斬。

translations.literal: When Commissioner Zhang Guangsi arrived, he impeached Yuansheng for merely trying to win over the enemy by appeasement, dismissed him, and had him arrested and sent to the capital; he was sentenced to death for delaying military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guangsi impeached Yuansheng for empty appeasement, stripped him, and condemned him to death for military delay.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，上命貸其死，賜副將銜，赴西路軍營效力。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong the Emperor ordered his life spared, granted him the rank of lieutenant colonel, and sent him to the western army to redeem himself.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 1 his life was spared; he was given lieutenant colonel rank on the western front.

sentences.zh: 三年，卒，上深惜之，加總兵銜，賜祭葬。

translations.literal: In the third year he died; the Emperor deeply regretted it, added regional commander rank, and granted funeral sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he died; the throne mourned him, raised him posthumously to regional commander, and granted funeral rites.

sentences.zh: 子尚德，初從元生至雲南，入伍，授千總。

translations.literal: His son Shangde had first followed Yuansheng to Yunnan, entered the army, and was appointed company commander.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shangde had followed him to Yunnan and become a company commander.

sentences.zh: 烏蒙既克，齎疏奏捷，上命以游擊題補，補雲南鶴麗右營游擊，遷奇兵營參將。

translations.literal: After Wuman was taken, he carried the victory memorial; the Emperor ordered him nominated for major; he was appointed major of the Heli right battalion in Yunnan and was promoted to colonel of the Odd Battalions.
translations.idiomatic: After Wuman fell he bore the victory report and was made Heli major, then Odd Battalions colonel.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，廣泗奏尚德奉檄從征，因父獲譴，黽勉自效。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong Guangsi reported that Shangde, under orders for the campaign, strove diligently because his father had been punished.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 1 Guangsi noted Shangde's zeal despite his father's disgrace.

sentences.zh: 擢貴州清江協副將，調定廣協。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Guizhou Qingjiang deputy commander and transferred to Dingguang.
translations.idiomatic: He became Qingjiang deputy commander, then moved to Dingguang.

sentences.zh: 三年，討平定番州屬姑盧寨苗。

translations.literal: In the third year he suppressed the Gulu stockade Miao under Dingfan prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he pacified the Gulu Miao of Dingfan.

sentences.zh: 以父憂歸，起湖南辰州副將。

translations.literal: He returned on his father's mourning and was recalled to be Chenzhou deputy commander in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death he was recalled as Chenzhou deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 遷總兵，歷宜昌、涼州、臨元、古州諸鎮。

translations.literal: He was promoted to regional commander and served in succession at Yichang, Liangzhou, Linyuan, and Guzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to regional commander at Yichang, Liangzhou, Linyuan, and Guzhou in turn.

sentences.zh: 十三年，討大金川，命從軍。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, when the Great Jinchuan was attacked, he was ordered to join the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he joined the Great Jinchuan campaign.

sentences.zh: 尋為總督張允隨劾擾民虐兵，坐奪官。

translations.literal: Soon Governor-General Zhang Yunsui impeached him for harassing the people and abusing the troops; he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Zhang Yunsui impeached him for oppressing civilians and troops, and he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，賜副將銜，赴西路軍營效力。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was granted lieutenant colonel rank and sent to the western army to redeem himself.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he was given lieutenant colonel rank on the western front.

sentences.zh: 以送羊赴軍多斃，奪官責償，遣回籍。

translations.literal: Because many sheep he delivered to the army died en route, he was dismissed, ordered to compensate, and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: Sheep he sent to the army died in transit; he was fined, dismissed, and sent home.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 董芳，陝西咸寧人。

translations.literal: Dong Fang was a native of Xianning in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Fang came from Xianning in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 初入伍，隸督標。

translations.literal: He first entered the army and served under the governor's standard.
translations.idiomatic: He enlisted in the governor's brigade.

sentences.zh: 中式武舉，補千總。

translations.literal: Having passed the military provincial examination, he was appointed company commander.
translations.idiomatic: As a military licentiate he became a company commander.

sentences.zh: 雍正二年，師徵青海，從副都統達鼐等追獲丹津琿台吉及其孥，並羅卜藏丹津女兄。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongzheng, when the army campaigned in Qinghai, he followed Vice Commander-in-chief Datang and others in pursuing and capturing Danjin Huitaiji and his family, as well as the sister of Luobuzang Danjin.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 2, on the Qinghai campaign, he helped Datang capture Danjin Huitaiji's family and Luobuzang Danjin's sister.

sentences.zh: 四年，超授三等侍衛，出為直隸正定鎮標游擊，累遷雲南臨元鎮總兵。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was specially promoted to third-rank bodyguard and went out as major of the Zhengding garrison in Zhili; he was repeatedly promoted to Linyuan regional commander in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he became third-rank bodyguard, then Zhengding major, then Linyuan commander in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 十一年，思茅土酋刁興國等為亂，芳與提督蔡成貴等率師討之，擒興國及助亂土目楊昌祿等，斬三千六百餘人，降四萬二千六百餘人。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the Simao native chieftain Diao Xingguo and others rebelled; Fang with Commander Cai Chenggui and others led troops to suppress them, captured Xingguo and the aiding native headman Yang Changlu, beheaded more than 3,600, and accepted the surrender of more than 42,600.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year Simao chieftain Diao Xingguo rebelled; Fang and Cai Chenggui killed 3,600 and accepted 42,600 surrenders.

sentences.zh: 總督高其倬留芳搜餘黨，悉平之。

translations.literal: Governor-General Gao Qisuo kept Fang to hunt the remaining partisans; all were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Qisuo kept him to mop up rebels until the region was quiet.

sentences.zh: 十二年，擢湖廣提督。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was promoted to Hunan provincial military commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he became Hunan commander.

sentences.zh: 十三年，貴州九股苗為亂，授雲南提督哈元生揚威將軍，芳副將軍，率師討之。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year the Jiugu Miao of Guizhou rebelled; Yunnan Commander Ha Yuansheng was made General Yangwei and Fang made deputy general to lead troops in suppression.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year the Jiugu Miao rose; Yuansheng became General Yangwei and Fang his deputy.

sentences.zh: 尋命尚書張照總理撫定苗疆，亂未定，高宗即位，授張廣泗為經略，視師。

translations.literal: Soon Minister Zhang Zhao was ordered to take overall charge of pacifying the Miao frontier; before the disorder was settled the Gaozong Emperor acceded and appointed Zhang Guangsi commissioner to supervise the army.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhao was put over Miao affairs; before peace came Qianlong enthroned Zhang Guangsi as commissioner.

sentences.zh: 廣泗劾芳駐軍八弓，依附張照，與元生互訐，師集數月，剿撫初無端緒。

translations.literal: Guangsi impeached Fang for stationing his army at Bagong, relying on Zhang Zhao, and mutually impeaching Yuansheng; the army gathered for months yet suppression and appeasement at first had no clear plan.
translations.idiomatic: Guangsi charged Fang with camping at Bagong, clinging to Zhang Zhao, feuding with Yuansheng, and achieving nothing for months.

sentences.zh: 奪芳官，逮京師。

translations.literal: Fang was dismissed and arrested and sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Fang was stripped and brought to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，王大臣會鞫，擬發邊遠充軍，上命寬之，以副將發雲南。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong princes and ministers jointly tried the case and proposed exile to the remote frontier as soldier; the Emperor ordered leniency and sent him out as lieutenant colonel in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 1 the joint trial proposed frontier exile; the Emperor lightened the sentence to Yunnan lieutenant colonel.

sentences.zh: 遭父憂，服除，署劍川協副將。

translations.literal: He suffered his father's death; when mourning ended he served as acting Jianchuan deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's mourning he acted as Jianchuan deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 擢總兵，歷楚姚、昭通二鎮。

translations.literal: He was promoted to regional commander and served in succession at Chuyao and Zhaotong.
translations.idiomatic: He became regional commander at Chuyao and Zhaotong in turn.

sentences.zh: 遭母憂，十三年，召赴京師，賜孔雀翎。

translations.literal: He suffered his mother's death; in the thirteenth year he was summoned to the capital and granted a peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's death, in the thirteenth year he was called to court and given a peacock plume.

sentences.zh: 命從征大金川，即授四川重慶總兵。

translations.literal: He was ordered to join the campaign against Great Jinchuan and at once appointed Chongqing regional commander in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the Great Jinchuan war as Chongqing commander.

sentences.zh: 經略訥親檄芳助總兵莽阿納等攻克普瞻左樑及阿利山梁碉卡。

translations.literal: Commissioner Necin ordered Fang to assist Regional Commander Mangana and others in taking the Puzhan left ridge and the Ali Mountain ridge blockhouses.
translations.idiomatic: Necin had him help Mangana take the Puzhan and Ali Mountain blockhouses.

sentences.zh: 又從提督岳鍾琪攻木耳金岡，奪土卡三、水卡一。

translations.literal: He also followed Commander Yue Zhongqi in attacking Mu'erjingang, seizing three earth forts and one water fort.
translations.idiomatic: With Yue Zhongqi he took three earth forts and one water fort at Mu'erjingang.

sentences.zh: 十四年，大金川事定，芳赴鎮，疏陳考察營汛，修補器械，並以地當黔、楚要衝，密訪侂嚕邪教，復發存庫米折借濟貧兵，上命諸事盡心料理。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, when the Great Jinchuan affair was settled, Fang went to his post and memorialized on inspecting garrisons, repairing weapons, and because the place lay on a vital route between Guizhou and Huguang, secretly investigating the Taolu cult; he also proposed issuing stored grain loans to poor soldiers; the Emperor ordered him to handle all matters with full care.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, after Jinchuan fell, he inspected posts, repaired arms, probed the Taolu sect on the Guizhou-Huguang frontier, and loaned grain to poor troops as ordered.

sentences.zh: 尋調建昌鎮。

translations.literal: He was soon transferred to Jianchang command.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon moved to Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 敘平大金川功，加左都督。

translations.literal: For merit in pacifying Great Jinchuan he was advanced to Left Commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: For the Jinchuan victory he was raised to Left Commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 十五年，西藏硃爾墨特、那木扎爾謀叛，既誅，其黨羅布藏扎什等為亂，總督策楞、提督岳鍾琪師入藏，命芳督兵策應。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year the Tibetan Zhuer Mot and Namuzhaer plotted rebellion; after they were executed their partisan Luobuzang Zhashi and others made trouble; Governor-General Celeng and Commander Yue Zhongqi led troops into Tibet; Fang was ordered to direct troops in support.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year Tibetan rebels Zhuer Mot and Namuzhaer were killed; their follower Luobuzang Zhashi rose; Celeng and Yue Zhongqi entered Tibet while Fang supported them.

sentences.zh: 十九年，調松潘鎮，擢貴州提督。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was transferred to Songpan command and promoted to Guizhou provincial military commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he became Songpan commander, then Guizhou commander.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，卒。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twenty-second year.

sentences.zh: 查弼納，完顏氏，滿洲正黃旗人。

translations.literal: Zhabina, of the Wanyan clan, was a bannerman of the Manchu Plain Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Zhabina of the Wanyan clan served in the Plain Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 祖愛音布，事世祖為戶部理事官，考滿，授拖沙喇哈番。

translations.literal: His grandfather Aiyinbu served the Shizu Emperor as a director in the Board of Revenue; when his term was completed he was granted tuosha lahafan.
translations.idiomatic: Grandfather Aiyinbu was a Revenue director under Shizu and earned tuosha lahafan.

sentences.zh: 以其孫觀音保襲，恩詔進三等阿達哈哈番。

translations.literal: His grandson Guanyinbao inherited the rank, and by grace edict it was advanced to third-rank adaha fan.
translations.idiomatic: Grandson Guanyinbao inherited, advanced by grace to third-rank adaha fan.

sentences.zh: 查弼納，觀音保弟也，襲世職，管佐領。

translations.literal: Zhabina was Guanyinbao's younger brother; he inherited the hereditary office and managed an assistant banner captaincy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhabina, Guanyinbao's brother, inherited the post and led an assistant captaincy.

sentences.zh: 康熙四十七年，授吏部郎中，三遷兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the forty-seventh year of Kangxi he was appointed director in the Board of Civil Appointments and was promoted three times to vice minister of the Board of War.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 47 he became a Civil Appointments director and rose to War vice minister.

sentences.zh: 六十一年，授江南江西總督。

translations.literal: In the sixty-first year he was appointed governor-general of Jiangnan and Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 61 he became Jiangnan-Jiangxi governor-general.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，台灣硃一貴餘黨溫上貴糾江西棚民掠萬載、新昌。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng, Wen Shanggui, a remnant of Zhu Yigui's Taiwan faction, incited Jiangxi shed-dwellers to plunder Wanzai and Xinchang.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 1, Taiwan rebel remnant Wen Shanggui stirred Jiangxi shed people to raid Wanzai and Xinchang.

sentences.zh: 亂定，大學士白潢、尚書張廷玉並疏議安輯棚民，下查弼納詳議。

translations.literal: After the disorder was settled, Grand Secretary Bai Huang and Minister Zhang Tingyu both memorialized on settling the shed-dwellers, and the matter was referred to Zhabina for detailed deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: When order returned, Bai Huang and Zhang Tingyu proposed shed-dweller policy; Zhabina was told to draft details.

sentences.zh: 查弼納奏：「江西界連福建、湖廣、廣東諸省，地曠山深，民無力開墾，招流民藝麻種靛。

translations.literal: Zhabina memorialized: "Jiangxi borders Fujian, Huguang, and Guangdong; the land is broad and the mountains deep; the people lack strength to open fields and have recruited floating population to grow hemp and indigo.
translations.idiomatic: Zhabina wrote: "Jiangxi touches Fujian, Huguang, and Guangdong; in its wild hills settlers grow hemp and indigo.

sentences.zh: 以其棚居，名曰'棚民'。

translations.literal: Because they live in sheds, they are called 'shed people.'
translations.idiomatic: They live in sheds, hence the name shed people.

sentences.zh: 安業日久，驅令回籍，必且生事。

translations.literal: Having long settled, if driven back to their native places they will surely make trouble.
translations.idiomatic: After long settlement, expulsion would breed unrest.

sentences.zh: 當編保甲，千戶以上，駐將吏稽察。

translations.literal: They should be organized into baojia; where households exceed a thousand, officers should be stationed to inspect.
translations.idiomatic: Register them in baojia; above a thousand households, post officers to watch them.

sentences.zh: 編冊後，續到流移，不得容隱。

translations.literal: After registration, later arrivals must not be concealed.
translations.idiomatic: Once listed, new migrants must not be hidden.

sentences.zh: 其讀書向學及有膂力者，得入籍應試。」

translations.literal: Those who study or have strength may enter local registration and sit for examinations."
translations.idiomatic: Students and strong men may gain household status and take exams."

sentences.zh: 下部議行。

translations.literal: The ministry deliberated and carried it out.
translations.idiomatic: The Board approved.

sentences.zh: 二年，奏言私鹽責所在州縣嚴捕，停駐防兵巡緝。

translations.literal: In the second year he memorialized that private salt should be strictly seized by the local prefectures and counties, and that garrison troops should cease salt patrols.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he urged counties to suppress private salt and end garrison patrols.

sentences.zh: 又奏言太湖跨數郡為盜藪，請移參將駐洞庭東山，周村、鐵橋、鮎魚口、馬跡山、黿山、東山、鳳山、吳溜設汛駐兵。

translations.literal: He also memorialized that Lake Tai, spanning several prefectures, was a robbers' nest, and asked that a lieutenant colonel be moved to garrison Dongshan in Lake Dongting, with garrison troops at Zhoucun, Tieqiao, Nianyukou, Majishan, Yuanshan, Dongshan, Fengshan, and Wuliu.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked for a colonel on Lake Tai's Dongshan and posts at Zhoucun, Tieqiao, Nianyukou, Majishan, Yuanshan, Dongshan, Fengshan, and Wuliu.

sentences.zh: 又奏言江南賦重事繁，請改六安、太倉、潁、泗、廬、邳、海、通諸州為直隸州，蘇、松、常三府增設元和、震澤、昭文、新陽、寶山、鎮洋、奉賢、金山、福泉、南匯、陽湖、金匱、荊溪諸縣。

translations.literal: He also memorialized that because Jiangnan's taxes were heavy and affairs numerous, he asked that Lu'an, Taicang, Ying, Si, Lu, Pi, Hai, and Tong be made directly governed prefectures, and that Yuanhe, Zhenze, Zhaowen, Xinyang, Baoshan, Zhenyang, Fengxian, Jinshan, Fuquan, Nanhui, Yanghu, Jinkui, and Jingxi counties be added to Suzhou, Songjiang, and Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed elevating eight prefectures and adding fourteen counties to lighten Suzhou, Songjiang, and Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 上既譴廉親王允禩，以貝勒蘇努、尚書隆科多等結黨亂政，詢查弼納。

translations.literal: The Emperor had already censured Prince Lian Yin Si; because Prince Su Nu, Minister Longkodo, and others formed factions and disturbed government, Zhabina was questioned.
translations.idiomatic: After Prince Lian Yin Si was punished, the throne questioned Zhabina about Su Nu, Longkodo, and their faction.

sentences.zh: 詔八至，查弼納不以實奏。

translations.literal: Eight edicts arrived, yet Zhabina did not report truthfully.
translations.idiomatic: Eight imperial orders came, but Zhabina concealed the truth.

sentences.zh: 四年，召詣京師，上親詰之，猶堅執不肯言。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was summoned to the capital; the Emperor questioned him in person, yet he still stubbornly refused to speak.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was called to court and still would not confess.

sentences.zh: 命奪官，下王大臣會鞫，乃具言蘇努與阿靈阿、揆敘、鄂倫岱、阿爾松阿結黨，欲戴允禩致大位，及隆科多交結揆敘、阿靈阿狀。

translations.literal: He was dismissed and tried by princes and ministers; only then did he fully report that Su Nu with Alingga, Kuaixu, Olondai, and Ersongga formed a faction to place Yin Si on the throne, and the dealings of Longkodo with Kuaixu and Alingga.
translations.idiomatic: Stripped and tried by princes, he revealed Su Nu's plot to enthrone Yin Si and Longkodo's ties with Kuaixu and Alingga.

sentences.zh: 王大臣擬查弼納罪斬，上諭曰：「查弼納本後進，畏附權勢。

translations.literal: The princes proposed death for Zhabina; the Emperor instructed: "Zhabina was originally a latecomer who feared and clung to power.
translations.idiomatic: Princes sought his death; the Emperor said: "Zhabina was a newcomer who clung to power.

sentences.zh: 朕昨言及聖祖，查弼納痛器不止，尚有良心，可免其罪。」

translations.literal: When I spoke yesterday of the Sacred Ancestor, Zhabina wept without cease; he still has conscience — his crime may be pardoned."
translations.idiomatic: When I mentioned the Kangxi Emperor yesterday he wept endlessly; he still has a heart — spare him."

sentences.zh: ​​尋授內務府總管、鑲紅旗漢軍都統，擢吏部尚書，協理兵部。

translations.literal: He was soon appointed superintendent of the Imperial Household Department and commander-in-chief of the Bordered Red Chinese Banner, was promoted to minister of Civil Appointments, and assisted in the Board of War.
translations.idiomatic: He became Household superintendent, Bordered Red Chinese commander, War minister, and War assistant.

sentences.zh: 五年，以濫保郎中舒伸，降級。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, for indiscriminately recommending Director Shushen, he was demoted in rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was demoted for recommending Director Shushen.

sentences.zh: 旋授兵部尚書。

translations.literal: He was soon appointed minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became War minister.

sentences.zh: 七年，師徵準噶爾，靖邊大將軍傅爾丹出北路，寧遠大將軍岳鍾琪出西路，查弼納赴肅州督西路軍需。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the army campaigned against the Dzungars; Pacification General of the Frontier Fu Erdan marched on the northern route and Pacification General of Pacifying the Distant Yue Zhongqi on the western route; Zhabina went to Suzhou to supervise western-route supplies.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, as Fu Erdan marched north and Yue Zhongqi west, Zhabina managed western supplies at Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 八年，召入覲，授副將軍，佐傅爾丹出北路。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was summoned for audience and appointed deputy general to assist Fu Erdan on the northern route.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was made Fu Erdan's deputy on the northern route.

sentences.zh: 九年六月，噶爾丹策零大舉入犯，傅爾丹中敵間，欲及敵未集先發，查弼納亦頗信之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the ninth year Galdan Tsering invaded in force; Fu Erdan fell for enemy disinformation and wished to strike before the foe gathered; Zhabina also largely believed it.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year's sixth month Galdan Tsering invaded; Fu Erdan, deceived, wanted a preemptive strike; Zhabina agreed.

sentences.zh: 師進，查弼納偕傅爾丹督兵繼之，至庫列圖嶺，入谷遇敵伏，師敗績。

translations.literal: The army advanced; Zhabina with Fu Erdan followed with troops; when they reached Kuletu Ridge and entered the valley they met an ambush and the army was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: They marched to Kuletu Ridge, were ambushed in the pass, and routed.

sentences.zh: 移軍和通呼爾哈諾爾，師大潰。

translations.literal: The army moved to Khurung Gol Nor; the army collapsed in great rout.
translations.idiomatic: At Khurung Gol Nor the army broke completely.

sentences.zh: 查弼納與傅爾丹及副將軍巴賽收餘兵四千，設營護輜重，且戰且行，渡哈爾噶納河。

translations.literal: Zhabina with Fu Erdan and Deputy General Basai gathered the remaining 4,000 troops, encamped to protect baggage, fought as they marched, and crossed the Khargana River.
translations.idiomatic: Zhabina, Fu Erdan, and Basai rallied 4,000 men, guarded the baggage train, fought retreating, and crossed the Khargana.

sentences.zh: 敵追至，查弼納躍馬舞刀潰圍出，與傅爾丹相失，慮以陷帥得罪，曰：「吾罪當死，蒙恩幸得生。

translations.literal: The enemy pursued; Zhabina leaped on his horse and fought his way out with his blade; he lost Fu Erdan and, fearing guilt for abandoning his commander, said: "My crime deserves death; by grace I have been spared.
translations.idiomatic: Pursued, Zhabina cut his way out, lost Fu Erdan, and said: "I deserve death yet was spared.

sentences.zh: 頒白之年，豈可復對獄吏？」

translations.literal: In the years when white hair is distributed, how can I face prison clerks again?"
translations.idiomatic: At my age, how can I face the judges again?"

sentences.zh: 遂復入陣，死。

translations.literal: He then reentered the battle line and died.
translations.idiomatic: He rode back into the fight and died.

sentences.zh: 巴賽亦求傅爾丹不得，趨敵力戰死。

translations.literal: Basai also could not find Fu Erdan, charged the enemy, and fought to the death.
translations.idiomatic: Basai, unable to find Fu Erdan, charged the foe and fell.

sentences.zh: 巴賽，鄭親王濟爾哈朗孫也，敵旌其黃帶以示師。

translations.literal: Basai was grandson of Prince Zheng Jirhala; the enemy displayed his yellow sash to the army.
translations.idiomatic: Basai was Prince Zheng Jirhala's grandson; the enemy waved his yellow sash.

sentences.zh: 參贊馬爾薩至紅石岩遇敵，中槍死。

translations.literal: Assistant Maersai reached Hongshiyan, met the enemy, was shot, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Maersai met the enemy at Hongshiyan and was shot dead.

sentences.zh: 達福，瓜爾佳氏，滿洲鑲黃旗人，鼇拜孫也。

translations.literal: Dafu, of the Guwalgiya clan, was a bannerman of the Manchu Bordered Yellow Banner and grandson of Oboi.
translations.idiomatic: Dafu of the Guwalgiya clan, Oboi's grandson, served in the Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 康熙五十二年，聖祖追錄鼇拜戰功，賜一等阿思哈尼哈番。

translations.literal: In the fifty-second year of Kangxi the Sacred Ancestor, recalling Oboi's battle merit, granted first-rank asihanihafan.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 52 the Emperor restored Oboi's honors as first-rank asihanihafan.

sentences.zh: 達福襲職，管佐領。

translations.literal: Dafu inherited the office and managed an assistant banner captaincy.
translations.idiomatic: Dafu inherited and led an assistant captaincy.

sentences.zh: 累擢正藍旗滿洲副都統。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Manchu lieutenant-general of the Plain Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Plain Blue Manchu lieutenant-general.

sentences.zh: 雍正五年，世宗以鼇拜功多，復一等公，仍以達福襲，授散秩大臣、前鋒統領。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yongzheng the Shizong Emperor, because Oboi's merit was great, restored the first-rank dukedom, still inherited by Dafu, and appointed him minister without portfolio and vanguard commandant.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 5 the throne restored Oboi's dukedom to Dafu and made him minister without portfolio and vanguard commandant.

sentences.zh: 七年，師將出，上召廷臣議，達福力諫。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, when the army was about to march out, the Emperor summoned court ministers for deliberation; Dafu strongly remonstrated.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, as war neared, Dafu argued fiercely against it at court.

sentences.zh: 上問故，達福曰：「噶爾丹策零狡黠，能得諸酋心為捍禦。

translations.literal: The Emperor asked the reason; Dafu said: "Galdan Tsering is cunning and can win the hearts of the chiefs to defend him.
translations.idiomatic: Asked why, Dafu said Galdan Tsering was cunning and held the chiefs' loyalty.

sentences.zh: ​​主少則諫易，將強則制專。

translations.literal: When the ruler is young remonstrance is easy; when the general is strong control is absolute.
translations.idiomatic: A young ruler hears advice; a strong general does as he pleases.

sentences.zh: 我數千里轉餉，攻彼效死之士，臣未見其可。」

translations.literal: We transport supplies thousands of li to attack men who fight to the death; I do not see how this can succeed."
translations.idiomatic: We haul grain thousands of li to fight men who will die; I see no victory.

sentences.zh: 辭益堅，上曰：「今使汝副傅爾丹以行，汝尚敢辭？」

translations.literal: His remonstrance grew firmer; the Emperor said: "Now I send you as Fu Erdan's deputy — do you still dare refuse?"
translations.idiomatic: He persisted; the Emperor said: "I make you Fu Erdan's deputy — will you still refuse?"

sentences.zh: 達福乃叩首出。

translations.literal: Dafu then kowtowed and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Dafu kowtowed and left.

sentences.zh: 師至邊，傅爾丹令達福將二千人駐庫卜克爾。

translations.literal: When the army reached the frontier, Fu Erdan ordered Dafu to lead 2,000 men garrisoned at Kubu Keer.
translations.idiomatic: At the frontier Fu Erdan posted Dafu with 2,000 men at Kubu Keer.

sentences.zh: 九年，傅爾丹出師，使達福偕定壽領第一隊，及移軍和通呼爾哈諾爾，晝夜力戰，殺敵千餘。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Fu Erdan took the field, had Dafu with Dingshou lead the first column, and when the army moved to Khurung Gol Nor they fought day and night and killed more than a thousand of the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Dafu and Dingshou led the first column; at Khurung Gol Nor they killed over a thousand in day-and-night fighting.

sentences.zh: 敵益大集，軍方移，達福殿，敵三萬餘環攻之，力戰，复殺敵千餘，沒於陣。

translations.literal: The enemy gathered in greater force; as the army was moving, Dafu covered the rear; more than thirty thousand of the enemy surrounded and attacked him; he fought fiercely and again killed more than a thousand before falling in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Surrounded by 30,000 as the army moved, Dafu in the rear killed another thousand and died.

sentences.zh: 定壽，赫舍里氏，滿洲正黃旗人。

translations.literal: Dingshou, of the Heseri clan, was a bannerman of the Manchu Plain Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Dingshou of the Heseri clan came from the Plain Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 初襲三等阿達哈哈番世職，授三等侍衛。

translations.literal: He first inherited a third-rank adaha fan hereditary office and was appointed third-rank bodyguard.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited third-rank adaha fan and became a third-rank bodyguard.

sentences.zh: 累遷正黃旗蒙古副都統。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Mongol lieutenant-general of the Plain Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Plain Yellow Mongol lieutenant-general.

sentences.zh: 康熙五十六年，以傅爾丹​​為振武將軍，出阿爾泰討策妄阿喇布坦，定壽將盛京、吉林兵千人當前鋒，屢破賊博囉布爾哈蘇、烏魯木齊。

translations.literal: In the fifty-sixth year of Kangxi, when Fu Erdan was made General Zhenwu and marched from Altai against Tsewang Arabtan, Dingshou led 1,000 troops from Fengtian and Jilin as vanguard and repeatedly defeated the enemy at Boluobuerhasu and Urumqi.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 56, under Fu Erdan against Tsewang Arabtan, Dingshou's 1,000 Fengtian and Jilin vanguard broke the foe at Boluobuerhasu and Urumqi.

sentences.zh: 雍正二年，授鑲黃旗蒙古都統。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongzheng he was appointed Mongol commander-in-chief of the Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 2 he became Bordered Yellow Mongol commander.

sentences.zh: 策妄阿喇布坦使乞和，定壽率兵還駐巴爾庫爾。

translations.literal: When Tsewang Arabtan sent envoys suing for peace, Dingshou led troops back to garrison Barkol.
translations.idiomatic: When Tsewang Arabtan sued for peace, Dingshou garrisoned Barkol.

sentences.zh: 部議阿爾泰當駐軍，授定壽阿爾泰駐防將軍。

translations.literal: The ministry deliberated that Altai should be garrisoned and appointed Dingshou Altai garrison general.
translations.idiomatic: The Board proposed an Altai garrison under Dingshou.

sentences.zh: 尋改命穆克登，而令定壽以都統銜參贊軍務。

translations.literal: The appointment was soon changed to Mukeden, while Dingshou was ordered to assist in military affairs with commander-in-chief rank.
translations.idiomatic: Mukeden replaced him, but Dingshou stayed as staff commander.

sentences.zh: 四年，率兵往扎布罕，召偕穆克登還京師。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he led troops to Zabhan and was summoned back to the capital with Mukeden.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he marched to Zabhan, then was recalled with Mukeden.

sentences.zh: 定壽奏留察罕蒐勒軍中自效。

translations.literal: Dingshou memorialized asking to remain at Chahan Suole to serve in the army.
translations.idiomatic: Dingshou asked to remain at Chahan Suole on active duty.

sentences.zh: 七年，大將軍傅爾丹自北路出師，命定壽仍以都統銜為軍營前鋒統領。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Grand General Fu Erdan marched out on the northern route; Dingshou was again ordered to serve as vanguard commander-in-chief of the camp with commander-in-chief rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Fu Erdan marched north; Dingshou again led the camp vanguard.

sentences.zh: 八年，傅爾丹令定壽以二千人駐伊克斯諾爾，護阿濟必濟卡倫。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Fu Erdan ordered Dingshou to garrison 2,000 men at Yikesinuoer to guard the Aji Biji pass.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Fu Erdan posted 2,000 men under Dingshou at Yikesinuoer.

sentences.zh: 九年，傅爾丹將出師，集諸將議，定壽曰：「噶爾丹策零聞我師至，斂兵觀變，是有謀也。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, when Fu Erdan was about to take the field, he assembled the generals for deliberation; Dingshou said: "When Galdan Tsering hears our army has come he will gather troops and watch developments — this shows he has a plan.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Dingshou warned that Galdan Tsering was watching and scheming.

sentences.zh: 不可信俘言輕進。」

translations.literal: Captives' words cannot be trusted for a rash advance."
translations.idiomatic: Prisoners' tales should not lure us forward.

sentences.zh: 傅爾丹責其懦，侍郎永國、副都統覺羅海蘭皆持不可，弗聽，師遂行。

translations.literal: Fu Erdan reproached him as cowardly; Vice Minister Yongguo and Lieutenant-general Gioro Hailan also objected, but he would not listen, and the army marched.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Erdan called him timid; Yongguo and Hailan objected in vain, and the army set out.

sentences.zh: 以定壽領第一隊，至扎克賽河，獲准噶爾兵二千餘；

translations.literal: Dingshou led the first column; at the Zhakesai River they captured more than 2,000 Dzungar troops;
translations.idiomatic: Dingshou's column took 2,000 Dzungars at the Zhakesai River;

sentences.zh: 及至庫列圖嶺，攻不克，將移軍和通呼爾哈諾爾。

translations.literal: when they reached Kuletu Ridge the attack failed, and they were about to move the army to Khurung Gol Nor.
translations.idiomatic: at Kuletu Ridge the assault failed, and they withdrew toward Khurung Gol Nor.

sentences.zh: 呼爾哈諾爾，華言大澤也。

translations.literal: Khurung Gol Nor means "great marsh" in Chinese.
translations.idiomatic: Khurung Gol Nor means Great Marsh in Chinese.

sentences.zh: 定壽詰傅爾丹曰：「違眾陷師，誰執其咎？」

translations.literal: Dingshou questioned Fu Erdan: "Defying the multitude and trapping the army — who will bear the blame?"
translations.idiomatic: Dingshou asked Fu Erdan who would answer for ignoring counsel and ruining the army.

sentences.zh: 傅爾丹默不語，定壽曰：「言在先，敢辭死乎？」

translations.literal: Fu Erdan was silent; Dingshou said: "I spoke first — how can I shrink from death?"
translations.idiomatic: Fu Erdan was silent; Dingshou said he had warned them and would not flee death.

sentences.zh: 軍甫移，敵大至，定壽督兵奮擊，所向披靡，乘勝入敵陣，風驟起，雨雹並至，師大敗。
