translations.literal: As the army had just moved, the enemy arrived in force; Dingshou directed the troops in fierce attack and swept all before him; pressing the advantage he entered the enemy formation; a sudden wind rose and rain and hail came together, and the army was utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: As they moved, the enemy struck; Dingshou charged until wind and hail broke the army.

sentences.zh: 敵圍定壽數重，定壽中鳥槍，猶力戰，相持竟夜。

translations.literal: The enemy surrounded Dingshou in many rings; Dingshou was struck by a musket ball yet still fought fiercely, holding out through the night.
translations.idiomatic: Ringed by the foe and shot, Dingshou fought through the night.

sentences.zh: 敵欲生致之，拔刀自剄，死於陣。

translations.literal: The enemy wished to take him alive; he drew his blade and cut his throat, dying in the battle line.
translations.idiomatic: When they tried to capture him alive, he cut his throat and fell.

sentences.zh: 副都統西爾賴令索倫兵赴援，兵潰，亦自殺。

translations.literal: Lieutenant-general Xilai ordered Solon troops to the rescue; the troops collapsed and he also killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Xilai's Solon relief broke; he killed himself.

sentences.zh: 素圖，富察氏，滿洲正黃旗人，費雅斯哈孫，素丹子也。

translations.literal: Sutu, of the Fuca clan, was a bannerman of the Manchu Plain Yellow Banner, grandson of Feiyasaha and son of Sudan.
translations.idiomatic: Sutu of the Fuca clan, Feiyasaha's grandson and Sudan's son, was Plain Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 素圖初名福列，襲二等阿達哈哈番，改名。

translations.literal: Sutu's original name was Fulie; he inherited second-rank adaha fan and changed his name.
translations.idiomatic: Born Fulie, he inherited second-rank adaha fan and renamed himself Sutu.

sentences.zh: 授護軍參領。

translations.literal: He was appointed guard commandant-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He became guard commandant-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 康熙五十四年，策妄阿喇布坦侵哈密，素圖與都統新泰率烏拉兵屯阿爾泰。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fourth year of Kangxi, when Tsewang Arabtan invaded Hami, Sutu with Commander-in-chief Xintai led Ula troops to garrison Altai.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 54, when Tsewang Arabtan struck Hami, Sutu and Xintai garrisoned Altai with Ula troops.

sentences.zh: 五十九年，從征西將軍祁里德出布勒罕，深入，斬敵伏四百餘。

translations.literal: In the fifty-ninth year he followed Western Campaign General Qilide out from Bulehan, advanced deep, and beheaded more than 400 of an ambushing enemy.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 59 he followed Qilide from Bulehan and killed 400 ambushers.

sentences.zh: 次鏗爾河，其宰桑色布騰據山拒，素圖督兵奮擊，大破之，色布騰以二千人降。

translations.literal: At the Kenger River their zaisang Seb Teng held the mountain in resistance; Sutu directed a fierce attack, routed them greatly, and Seb Teng surrendered with 2,000 men.
translations.idiomatic: At the Kenger River he stormed Seb Teng's hill position; Seb Teng surrendered with 2,000 men.

sentences.zh: 六十年，移軍巴爾庫爾，赴吐魯番督築城屯田。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year the army moved to Barkol; he went to Turfan to supervise building the city and opening military colonies.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 60 he moved to Barkol and built Turfan's garrison farms.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，從副將軍阿喇納駐布隆吉爾。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng he followed Deputy General Alana to garrison Bulongjier.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 1 he garrisoned Bulongjier with Alana.

sentences.zh: 二年，準噶爾犯邊，偕總兵孫繼宗擊之，敵敗走，乃城布隆吉爾。

translations.literal: In the second year the Dzungars raided the border; he with Regional Commander Sun Jizong attacked them; the enemy was defeated and fled, and they then walled Bulongjier.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he and Sun Jizong beat a border raid and walled Bulongjier.

sentences.zh: 復從副都統達鼐逐羅卜藏丹津至花海子，獲台吉丹津及其妻子，並招降台吉噶斯等。

translations.literal: He again followed Lieutenant-general Datang in pursuing Luobuzang Danjin to Huahaizi, captured taiji Danjin and his wife and children, and also won over taiji Gasi and others by surrender.
translations.idiomatic: With Datang he pursued Luobuzang Danjin to Huahaizi, took Danjin's family, and won Gasi's surrender.

sentences.zh: 上以方冬冰凍草枯，師奮勇遠征，下詔褒勉。

translations.literal: Because it was deep winter with ice and withered grass, yet the army had campaigned far in valor, an edict was issued commending them.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor praised their winter march in an edict.

sentences.zh: 擢寧夏左翼副都統。

translations.literal: He was promoted to left-wing lieutenant-general of Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: He became Ningxia left-wing lieutenant-general.

sentences.zh: 時素丹為寧夏將軍，年已老，上命素圖協理將軍。

translations.literal: At that time Sudan was Ningxia general and already old; the Emperor ordered Sutu to assist in managing the generalship.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sudan, aged Ningxia general, was assisted by Sutu.

sentences.zh: 尋命率西安滿洲兵二千從傅爾丹出北路，授參贊大臣。

translations.literal: He was soon ordered to lead 2,000 Xi'an Manchu troops following Fu Erdan on the northern route and was appointed assisting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He soon took 2,000 Xi'an Manchu troops north with Fu Erdan as assisting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 及庫列圖嶺之戰，素圖與副都統岱豪殺敵四百餘。

translations.literal: At the battle of Kuletu Ridge, Sutu with Lieutenant-general Dai Hao killed more than 400 of the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: At Kuletu Ridge Sutu and Dai Hao killed 400 enemies.

sentences.zh: 移軍和通呼爾哈諾爾，素圖與定壽及副都統常祿等據山梁之東，敵大至，素圖、常祿與歸化城副都統馬爾齊力御之，沒於陣。

translations.literal: When the army moved to Khurung Gol Nor, Sutu with Dingshou and Lieutenant-general Chang Lu and others held the eastern mountain ridge; the enemy came in force; Sutu, Chang Lu, and Guihuacheng Lieutenant-general Maerqi resisted with all their strength and fell in battle.
translations.idiomatic: At Khurung Gol Nor Sutu, Dingshou, Chang Lu, and Maerqi held the eastern ridge and died fighting.

sentences.zh: 侍郎永國、副都統覺羅海蘭、岱豪帳中自經死。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Yongguo, Lieutenant-general Gioro Hailan, and Dai Hao hanged themselves in their tents.
translations.idiomatic: Yongguo, Hailan, and Dai Hao hanged themselves in camp.

sentences.zh: 時諸將惟副都統德祿、承保從傅爾丹得出。

translations.literal: At that time among the generals only Lieutenant-generals Delu and Chengbao escaped with Fu Erdan.
translations.idiomatic: Only Delu and Chengbao escaped with Fu Erdan.

sentences.zh: 伯都訥副都統塔爾岱中槍穿脛，蒙古醫蒙以羊皮，三日始蘇。

translations.literal: Boduna Lieutenant-general Ta'erdai was shot through the calf; a Mongol doctor wrapped him in sheepskin, and after three days he revived.
translations.idiomatic: Ta'erdai of Boduna was shot through the calf; a Mongol doctor wrapped him in sheepskin and he revived after three days.

sentences.zh: 上令還伯都訥，塔爾岱言：「原從軍勦賊雪恥。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered him back to Boduna; Ta'erdai said: "I originally wished to follow the army to suppress bandits and wipe away disgrace.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered home, Ta'erdai said he wished to stay and fight.

sentences.zh: 若負罪而還，何顏見七十有七之老母？」

translations.literal: If I return bearing guilt, with what face can I see my seventy-seven-year-old mother?"
translations.idiomatic: How can I face my seventy-seven-year-old mother if I return in disgrace?"

sentences.zh: 上深嘉之，並賜塔爾岱及其母各白金千。

translations.literal: The Emperor deeply praised this and granted Ta'erdai and his mother each 1,000 taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor praised him and gave Ta'erdai and his mother 1,000 taels each.

sentences.zh: 參贊都統陳泰屯科布多河岸，聞敵至，退駐紮布韓，上命斬之。

translations.literal: Assistant Commissioner Commander-in-chief Chen Tai was stationed on the Ke'erduo riverbank; when he heard the enemy had come he withdrew to garrison Zhabuhan; the Emperor ordered him beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant Commissioner Chen Tai held the Ke'erduo bank but retreated to Zhabuhan when the enemy approached; the Emperor ordered his execution.

sentences.zh: 議卹查弼納、馬爾薩、素圖、覺羅海蘭，皆授拜他喇布勒哈番兼拖沙喇哈番；

translations.literal: It was deliberated to grant posthumous honors to Zhabina, Maersai, Sutu, and Gioro Hailan, each receiving batala buluhafan together with tuosha lahafan;
translations.idiomatic: Zhabina, Maersai, Sutu, and Gioro Hailan were each posthumously granted batala buluhafan with tuosha lahafan;

sentences.zh: 達福、岱豪、西彌賴、常祿、定壽、永國授拜他喇布勒哈番；

translations.literal: Dafu, Dai Hao, Ximilai, Chang Lu, Dingshou, and Yongguo were granted batala buluhafan;
translations.idiomatic: Dafu, Dai Hao, Ximilai, Chang Lu, Dingshou, and Yongguo received batala buluhafan;

sentences.zh: 餘並授拖沙喇哈番。

translations.literal: the rest were all granted tuosha lahafan.
translations.idiomatic: the others received tuosha lahafan.

sentences.zh: 查弼納、達福、定壽、素圖舊有世職，查弼納合為三等阿達哈哈番，定壽、素圖皆合為三等阿思哈尼哈番，達福以其孫別襲巴賽，追封簡親王，見鄭親王濟爾哈朗傳。

translations.literal: Zhabina, Dafu, Dingshou, and Sutu had former hereditary offices; Zhabina's were combined as third-rank adaha fan, Dingshou's and Sutu's both combined as third-rank asihanihafan; Dafu's grandson separately inherited for Basai, and [Basai] was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince Jian; see the biography of Prince Zheng Jirhala.
translations.idiomatic: Zhabina, Dafu, Dingshou, and Sutu all held hereditary ranks: Zhabina's merged into third-rank adaha fan, Dingshou's and Sutu's into third-rank asihanihafan; Dafu's grandson inherited separately for Basai, who was posthumously made Prince Jian — see the biography of Prince Zheng Jirhala.

sentences.zh: 論曰：西藏之師，噶爾弼深入奮戰，而功獨歸主將，番代遠戍，怏怏不欲行，殆以此歟？

translations.literal: The commentator says: In the Tibet campaign Garbi fought deep within enemy territory with great valor, yet the merit went solely to the commander-in-chief; when bannermen were rotated for distant garrison duty they were resentful and unwilling to go — was it perhaps for this reason?
translations.idiomatic: The historian remarks: Garbi stormed deep into Tibet, yet credit went to his commander alone; when banner troops were sent on distant rotations they went unwillingly — was that not the reason?

sentences.zh: 查克丹與額爾德尼昭之戰，常賚佐巴爾庫爾之師，元生、芳屢定亂苗，而元生尤著，卒以牽制坐使遷延。

translations.literal: Chakedan at the battle of Erdeni Zhao, Chang Lai assisting the Barkol army, Yuansheng and Fang repeatedly pacifying rebellious Miao — Yuansheng especially distinguished himself — yet in the end mutual obstruction caused delay.
translations.idiomatic: Chakedan won at Erdeni Zhao; Chang Lai served at Barkol; Yuansheng and Fang pacified the Miao again and again, Yuansheng most of all — yet factional strife still slowed the war.

sentences.zh: 查弼納敭歷已久，晚乃從軍，和通腦兒之敗，一軍盡覆，而主將獨逭重誅，抑又何也？

translations.literal: Zhabina had long experience in office and only late in life followed the army; at the defeat at Khurung Gol Nor the whole army was destroyed, yet the commander-in-chief alone escaped heavy punishment — how can this be explained?
translations.idiomatic: Zhabina was a veteran of long service who took the field only late in life; at Khurung Gol Nor the army was wiped out while the commander alone escaped severe punishment — what are we to make of that?
